Subject: Re: PII handling confirmation for prompts/outputs

Hi Sofia — thanks for the great questions. Below are concise, actionable answers mapped to each of your points. I’ll also populate the questionnaire you sent.

1) Hosted API (default behavior):
   - Prompts & outputs: By default, Redwood retains request/response payloads for 30 days for troubleshooting and abuse monitoring. These records are accessible only to authorized Redwood personnel and are encrypted at rest.
   - Opt-out: Customers can opt out of payload logging for their account; when disabled, prompts/outputs are not persisted beyond transient processing memory. Opt-out can be enabled via the Console or API and takes effect immediately for new requests.

2) Embeddings:
   - Persistence: Embeddings are persisted only when a customer explicitly writes them to our embeddings index (Create / Upsert operations). They are not stored by model inference alone.
   - Auto-deletion: Customers can configure retention policies (e.g., auto-delete after N days) for embedding indices in Dedicated and Private; for Hosted accounts, we can offer managed retention windows (default 365 days) and shorter windows by request (enterprise-tier).

3) Logging & redaction: 
   - Logs retained: Request metadata (timestamps, model, token count, response latency) is retained for 365 days for analytics. Full request/response payloads: default 30 days (see opt-out above).
   - Redaction: We provide an optional ingest-time PII redaction pipeline (regex & ML-based) that can be enabled per-account; the pipeline can strip or mask fields based on patterns you provide.
   - Encryption: Data is encrypted at rest; for Dedicated/Private customers we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) via KMS/HSM integrations.

4) Dedicated / Private options:
   - Control: Dedicated customers get configurable retention policies and the ability to disable payload logging at the instance level. Private (VPC / on-prem) customers have full control over persistence and can configure zero retention if required.
   - Residency: For Hosted accounts we store data in the region you select (US or EU). Dedicated/Private can be provisioned in EU, US, or on-premise in your cloud account.

5) Compliance evidence / DPA:
   - SOC2: Attached is a short SOC2 summary; we can provide the full report under an NDA.
   - DPA / DSR: We have a standard DPA; we can provide redlineable language and support custom terms for enterprise contracts.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

Quick notes / recommendations based on your use case:
- If you plan to send PHI in prompts, we recommend Dedicated or Private with BYOK and ingest-time redaction enabled.
- If you want to use Hosted but avoid storing prompts/outputs, enable payload logging opt-out and leverage automatic redaction rules.

Next steps: I’ll fill out your questionnaire and propose language for the DPA. Please let me know which deployment you prefer so we can provide exact SLOs and retention config examples.

— Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha@redwood-inference.com
